options: Compressing personal data to save storage
Removing or modifying personal information before sharing so that the people the data is about remain anonymous
Backing up personal data to an offsite location
Publishing personal data with the owner's consent
Converting personal data into a different file format
questions.explanation: Data Anonymisation hides the identity of a person so that it is undetectable, by removing or modifying personal information before sharing.

questions.stem: To which area of data practice are Data Anonymisation, Data Pseudonymisation and Data De-identification related?
questions.explanation: All three work the same way and are related to Data Privacy.

questions.stem: Which scenario is given as an example of when Data Anonymisation is required?
options: Sharing data with a development team while implementing a data solution
questions.explanation: Before sharing data with the development team, one must make sure it is anonymised so details such as name, contact number, address and credit card number are not exposed.

questions.stem: By whom is Data Anonymisation normally enforced?
questions.explanation: Data Anonymisation is normally enforced by regulatory bodies.

questions.stem: What can happen to an organisation that fails to anonymise data as required?
options: It receives a certificate of compliance
It faces heavy penalties and a bad reputation
questions.explanation: Not following anonymisation requirements can result in heavy penalties and a bad reputation for the organisation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a Data Anonymisation technique?
questions.explanation: The listed techniques include masking, pseudonymisation, generalisation, swapping, perturbation, synthetic data, shuffling, scrambling, encoding and de-identification; compression is not one of them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of Data Anonymisation?
options: Anonymised data cannot be used for marketing
Anonymised data takes up more storage
Anonymised data cannot be shared with development teams
Anonymised data is illegal in most countries
Anonymised data cannot be loaded into a database
questions.explanation: One disadvantage is that anonymised data cannot be used for marketing; another is that data migration testing may show mismatches.

questions.stem: Why can Data Anonymisation cause problems in a Data Migration project?
options: Because anonymised data is always larger
Because regulators forbid migrating anonymised data
Because migration tools cannot read anonymised files
Because migration projects normally require the original dataset for testing, so anonymisation can lead to mismatches
Because anonymisation deletes the source database
questions.explanation: Data Migration projects normally require the original dataset for testing, so anonymised data can lead to a mismatch.

questions.stem: Which technique is used in the Data Anonymisation before-and-after example in I Am Datapedia!?
questions.explanation: The example of Data Anonymisation uses the Data Swapping technique.

questions.stem: How do Data Anonymisation, Data Pseudonymisation and Data De-identification relate to one another?
options: They all work the same way and relate to Data Privacy
Only Data Anonymisation is enforced by regulators
Data Pseudonymisation is the opposite of Data Anonymisation
Data De-identification applies only to unstructured data
questions.explanation: Data Anonymisation, Data Pseudonymisation and Data De-identification all work the same way and are related to Data Privacy.
